messages:
maria: Heads up — prod-eu GPU pool started returning a bunch of Pending pods ~02:45 UTC. Errors show 0/12 nodes had free GPUs. Not a quota issue. Anyone else seeing this?

sam: yep, I noticed spikes in pending for batch-infer and rt-embed. `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -n prod | grep gpu` shows ~40 pending.

infra-bot: [03:07 UTC] Node gpu-eu-spot-7 preempted (spot eviction). Node gpu-eu-spot-3 preempted.

kevin: output from `kubectl describe pod prod/rt-embed-9f2` -> "0/24 nodes are available: 14 node(s) didn't have free GPUs, 6 node(s) didn't match nodeSelector." Also seeing scheduler predicate messages about MIG instance constraints.

olivia: Summary from node inventory: we have two GPU nodepools in eu: `gpu-eu-on-demand` (4 nodes, whole GPUs, A100) and `gpu-eu-spot` (8 nodes, some A100 nodes configured with MIG slices). Spot pool has been fluctuating because of evictions earlier this morning.

sam: That explains fragmentation — pods are requesting full `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` but many spot nodes have GPUs partitioned into MIG slices, so they don't advertise a full GPU. Scheduler treats them as unavailable for whole-GPU pods. When spot nodes go away, remaining nodes are full and CA isn't scaling up fast enough.

kevin: autoscaler logs show CA attempted scale-up but chose spot pool by expander config. autoscaler-bot: "Cluster Autoscaler: ScaleUp: group gpu-eu-spot desired: 5 -> 8 (reason: Unschedulable pods)." Then two spot nodes were evicted, dropping useful capacity and leaving small slices behind — classic binpacking fragmentation + preemption cascade.

maria: Ok. Two questions: short-term hotfix to clear pending pods, and medium-term config changes to prevent repeated fragmentation during spot churn.

olivia: Short-term options: 1) Temporarily increase `gpu-eu-on-demand` max size (we have headroom in the reserved budget) so CA can scale on-demand faster; 2) Add nodeAffinity/taints to route full-GPU critical pods to on-demand pool; 3) Roll a targeted `kubectl drain` of the remaining heavily-sliced spot nodes and cordon them until we can reconcile.

sam: I can flip the on-demand nodepool max from 4->8 and bump desired to 6, give CA room to add nodes. Command I ran: `gcloud container node-pools update gpu-eu-on-demand --max-nodes=8 --cluster=redwood-eu-prod` (GKE example).

kevin: Medium-term: label MIG-sliced nodes with `gpu.mig=true` and use a nodeSelector or nodeAffinity for pods that require whole GPUs. Also set CA expander to `least-waste` (instead of price/priority) so it prefers nodes that minimize leftover fractional GPUs. We should also enable `--balance-similar-node-groups` so CA evens out across pools.

olivia: Another medium-term: add a small dedicated reserved pool for latency-sensitive services (on-demand, pinned) — accept higher cost but avoid runtime preemption and binpack churn. For best-effort batch jobs we can keep using spot/mig-sliced nodes.

sam: Quick snippet to isolate whole-GPU pods: in prod scheduler policy use requiredAffinity: `nodeSelectorTerms: - matchExpressions: - {key: "gpu.mig", operator: "DoesNotExist"}`. That sends full-GPU pods only to non-MIG nodes.

kevin: We should also examine pod resource requests: some services request `nvidia.com/gpu: 0.5` via sharing libs — but K8s doesn't support fractional GPU unless using device-plugin sharing. Make sure teams are not relying on ad-hoc GPU-sharing leading to unschedulable placements.

maria: Action items: 
- sam: bump on-demand pool max and monitor CA scale events (+30m)
- olivia: label MIG nodes and coordinate with infra to add `gpu.mig=true` and patch daemonsets for deviceplugin detection
- kevin: change CA expander to least-waste and enable balance-similar-node-groups; propose reserved pool sizing for next infra sync
- everyone: add quick docs note about MIG vs whole-GPU placement for dev teams

infra-bot: [03:15 UTC] Created incident #INC-2026-453 for "EU GPU scheduling: fragmentation + spot evictions" and paged oncall.

maria: thanks — will follow up in the incident. If anyone has urgent pods, add `priorityClassName: high-priority-gpu` as temporary workaround so CA prioritizes scale-up for them. :thumbsup:

sam: on it. Running `kubectl patch deployment batch-infer -n prod -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"priorityClassName":"high-priority-gpu"}}}}'` now.

kevin: Also recommend adding a CA scale-up buffer (node-provisioning delay) to give CA time to react before spot nodes are heavily used.

olivia: 👍 will do the labels and open PR for scheduler policy.

maria: closing thread for now, keep updates in the incident. :white_check_mark:
